title: Test-driven development (TDD) with Claude Code
summary: Developer shows TDD loops with Claude Code using Playwright end-to-end and integration tests to let agents iterate unattended.

assertions.quote: why you should be using test-driven development when you are coding with AI

verdicts.note: Tests-first gives agents a target and limits test-cheating; evidence is mostly anecdotal and it does not suit all code (e.g. UI).

assertions.quote: take yourself out of the loop and to put tests, automated tests, there instead

verdicts.note: Agent benchmarks and practice consistently show verifiable feedback (tests, compilers) is the main driver of agent success.

assertions.quote: with AI, you really want to focus on the end-to-end tests and the integration tests

verdicts.note: Higher-level tests catch the cross-component errors agents make and become cheap to run unattended; unit tests still give fast, precise feedback. Plausible practitioner view, not measured.

assertions.quote: inside of testing.md, I have everything that the uh needs to know in order to run the playwright end-to-end tests

verdicts.note: Persistent instruction files measurably steer agent behavior; overlong or contradictory ones reduce adherence.
